title: Transport of inverse-limit acyclicity through compatible equivalences
statement: Let A, B, C and D be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian], with countable inverse limits in B and D whose limit functors are additive. Let EX : A ≌ C and EY : B ≌ D be equivalences, let P : A → B and Q : C → D be additive functors, and let P followed by EY be naturally isomorphic to EX followed by Q. Assume that, for every K-injective complex U of inverse sequences in C, every K-injective complex V of inverse sequences in D, and every quasi-isomorphism q from the levelwise Q-image of U to V, applying the ordinary inverse-limit functor gives a quasi-isomorphism. Here complexes and quasi-isomorphisms are as in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and K-injectivity is as in [def-pur-kinjective-complex]. Then the same property holds for P: if I and T are K-injective complexes of inverse sequences in A and B and j is a quasi-isomorphism from levelwise P(I) to T, the ordinary inverse-limit image of j is a quasi-isomorphism.

source.place: Tags 0A07 and 0D6E, invariance of the resolution acyclicity criterion under equivalences

proof.text: Whiskering EX and EY by the inverse-sequence index yields exact additive equivalences. They preserve quasi-isomorphisms. They preserve K-injective complexes because each is right adjoint to its exact inverse; use the already proved right-adjoint criterion.

Lift the given natural isomorphism first to inverse-sequence categories, using the canonical comparison for composition of right-whiskering, and then to cochain complexes, using mapHomologicalComplexCompIso. Precompose the image of j under the target equivalence by its inverse component. The resulting map j-prime is a quasi-isomorphism with the required source and target in the model categories.

Apply the assumed resolution criterion for Q to j-prime. A functor sends isomorphisms to isomorphisms. Cancel the inverse-limit image of the comparison isomorphism from this conclusion, obtaining the quasi-isomorphism for inverse limit after the target equivalence.

The target equivalence preserves inverse limits. Use preservesLimitNatIso to compare inverse limit followed by the target equivalence to its levelwise action followed by inverse limit. Quasi-isomorphisms are invariant under this natural isomorphism. Finally exact equivalences reflect quasi-isomorphisms, giving the inverse-limit image of the original j. No exactness of inverse limits is used.

theorem towerLimitAcyclicOfEquivalences
    {A : Type a} [Category.{av} A] [Abelian A]
    {B : Type b} [Category.{bv} B] [Abelian B]
    {C : Type c} [Category.{cv} C] [Abelian C]
    {D : Type d} [Category.{dv} D] [Abelian D]
    [HasLimitsOfShape ℕᵒᵖ B] [HasLimitsOfShape ℕᵒᵖ D]
    [(lim : (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ B) ⥤ B).Additive] [(lim : (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ D) ⥤ D).Additive]
    (EX : A ≌ C) (EY : B ≌ D) (P : A ⥤ B) [P.Additive]
    (Q : C ⥤ D) [Q.Additive] (em : P ⋙ EY.functor ≅ EX.functor ⋙ Q)
    (hq : ∀ (I : CochainComplex (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ C) ℤ), I.IsKInjective →
      ∀ (T : CochainComplex (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ D) ℤ), T.IsKInjective →
      ∀ (q : ((((Functor.whiskeringRight ℕᵒᵖ _ _).obj Q).mapHomologicalComplex
        (.up ℤ)).obj I) ⟶ T), QuasiIso q →
      QuasiIso (((lim : (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ D) ⥤ D).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).map q))
    (I : CochainComplex (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ A) ℤ) (hI : I.IsKInjective)
    (T : CochainComplex (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ B) ℤ) (hT : T.IsKInjective)
    (j : ((((Functor.whiskeringRight ℕᵒᵖ _ _).obj P).mapHomologicalComplex
      (.up ℤ)).obj I) ⟶ T) [QuasiIso j] :
    QuasiIso (((lim : (ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ B) ⥤ B).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).map j)
